body:
## Purpose

Pratik's direction (2026-11-01): "All these missing live skills also should be added to AEP." The purpose of maintaining skills in AEP, in his framing, is to version and upgrade them here so that other Muse agents and the current environment can pull skills from AEP and stay in sync. This PR adds every skill that existed only in the live tree (`~/workspace/custom-skills/`) and had no counterpart under `skills/`, so the repo snapshot set now covers the full live set (minus one held-out item, below).

## What this does

- Copies **18 skills** from live into `skills/<name>/`, byte-exact, minus the standing exclusions from `.github/skills-sync-scope.txt`.
- Adds all 18 names to the scope file's `[skills]` section (51 → 69; additions only — header and exclusion sections untouched).
- Regenerates `.github/skills-manifest.sha256` with the checker (95 → 152 entries); `check_skills_manifest.py --check` passes. All three changes land together, as the freshness gate requires.

## Per-skill outcomes

| Skill | Files copied | Exclusions |
|---|---|---|
| diagnosing-superpowers | 20 | skill.yaml (path rule) |
| direct_drive_execution | 2 | skill.yaml (path rule) |
| domain-modeling | 4 | — |
| excalibur-quest | 5 | skill.yaml (path rule) |
| finishing-a-development-branch | 1 | skill.yaml (path rule) |
| grill-me | 2 | — |
| grill-with-docs | 2 | — |
| handoff | 2 | — |
| neurogenesis | 2 | — |
| open-code-review-delegate | 1 | — |
| overseer | 4 | skill.yaml (path rule) |
| paperthin-attribution | 3 | — |
| plan-review-integrator | 1 | skill.yaml (path rule) |
| planning-wringer | 1 | — |
| receiving-code-review | 1 | skill.yaml (path rule) |
| retro | 2 | — |
| using-git-worktrees | 1 | skill.yaml (path rule) |
| wizard | 3 | — |

Total: 57 files copied, 8 excluded (all `skill.yaml`, whose meaning differs between the two homes — live import descriptor vs repo registry entry). No `.superpowers/` files and no `/home/hatch`-literal files existed in the set, so no content-rule exclusions fired.

**Held out:** `recovered-skill-notes` — read before deciding: it is a recovery-notes store (hash-named recovered fragments, a write-lock, and a SKILL.md that itself says to mine the contents into real skills and retire the entry), not a usable skill. It was excluded on that basis; Pratik can overrule and it can be added the same way.

## Verification

- Gitleaks v8.24.3 (checksum-verified per this repo's CI procedure, repo `.gitleaks.toml`) over everything copied before committing: **no leaks**.
- Checker tests: 8/8 (`scripts/tests/test_skills_manifest.py`); `test_skill_invocation_matches_cli`: passes.
- Independent whole-branch review: **APPROVED-WITH-NOTES** — full-set byte comparison (57 expected = 57 committed, 0 differences, not spot-checks only), exclusion completeness re-derived from live, scope/manifest consistency re-run, and a break-the-behavior test (one flipped byte in a throwaway copy → checker fails with hash mismatch, exit 1).

## Notes from review (recorded, not fixed — copied content is never edited)

- `skills/direct_drive_execution/.write-lock` (0 bytes) was copied byte-exact and **kept**: the scope file is the single source for exclusions, it violates none, and it is inert in a snapshot. If it should go, the route is a scope-file `[exclude-paths]` PR, not an ad-hoc omission (the next sync would otherwise re-add it).
- `paperthin-attribution/` contains no SKILL.md — it is the attribution/vendoring record (LICENSE, NOTICE, README) for the paperthin skills the repo already carries; included deliberately on that basis.
- Two copied skills carry environment-coupled prose (`direct_drive_execution` links an `/opt/muse/...` runtime path; `neurogenesis` is written against this environment's memory tooling). Recorded here; content left exactly as live has it.

## Governance status — superseded by the D4 revision (2026-11-01)

Since this PR was opened, Pratik approved a revision of decision D4 (2026-11-01) and directed its propagation after a planning-wringer review. Under the revision, AEP's default branch is the canonical version of record for skills and the live skills are the executing working copy; the sync machinery gains a drift-direction guard so repo-side changes are never overwritten or resurrected by the sync. Full record: `decision-4-revised-2026-11-01.md` in the AEP goal workspace (`hidden_files/plans/sdd-2026-10-25-codex-countermeasures/`), with the wringer plan at `hidden_files/plans/2026-11-01-d4-revision-propagation-plan.md`. This PR's merge remains Pratik's word; whichever of PR #84 / PR #85 merges second must be rebased with its manifest regenerated by `check_skills_manifest.py --write`, never hand-merged.



---

## Addendum 2026-11-02 — quest_helper.js fixed at the source (commit 62fc603)

The three Codex findings on this PR were all in the copied `skills/excalibur-quest/scripts/quest_helper.js` and pre-existed in the live skill. Per the revised D4 flow — and the repo owner's explicit direction — the file was fixed at the live source first, then re-copied byte-exact into this branch (live and repo copies now share sha256 `b651b8c946274037a6487420b96dcb9d9b12365041cd46cd6f2af069292cc287`); the manifest was regenerated for that single file.

- **P1 (shell injection):** `gh` and `dolt` are now invoked via `execFileSync` argument arrays in `runSync`, `QuestDB.loadQuest`, and `QuestDB.saveQuest`. Review-derived finding titles and quest JSON reach the process only as literal argv elements — no shell is involved. The only remaining `execSync` calls are static strings with no interpolation.
- **P2 (Dolt JSON corruption):** the SQL, including the quest JSON, is passed as a single argv element, so its double quotes survive; the pre-existing SQL `''`-escaping is unchanged and now actually effective.
- **P2 (unserialized JSON store):** the JSON fallback now holds an exclusive lockfile (`quest_db.json.lock`, atomic `wx` create, 30 s stale drop) across its read-modify-write; all mutations route through the locked path.

Evidence: each defect was reproduced pre-fix with stub executables (an injected title created a marker file during `sync`; Dolt-stored JSON lost its quotes and the quest became unloadable; 4 concurrent `init`s kept only 2 quests) and verified fixed post-fix (no marker, title received literally; quest round-trips to COMPLETED; 4/4 quests survive, including against a seeded 20k-entry store). An independent review of the fix returned APPROVED-WITH-NOTES: two low notes, recorded here — the 30 s stale-lock bound is an implicit cap on a single write's duration (the read-modify-write is sub-second at this store's scale), and `issueId` remains interpolated into SQL strings (operator-supplied CLI input, unchanged by this fix and outside the review-data injection class).


---

## Addendum 2026-11-03 — round 2: the three re-review P2s fixed at the source; branch brought current with main

The re-review of 62fc603 opened three further P2 threads, all pre-existing defects in this batch's copied content. The repo owner directed: fix all three at the source and re-copy. Done in commit ae872dd; live and repo copies are byte-identical for all three files.

- **Seat reclaim (quest_helper.js):** acquirers now record their PID in an `owner` file inside the seat directory; a seat is reclaimed iff its owner fails `kill(pid, 0)` with ESRCH, and a seat with no ownership record is reclaimable only once its directory is >30 s old (the same staleness rule as the store lock), so a mid-acquisition seat cannot be stolen. PID reuse and zombie owners both fail safe (the seat reads as held, never wrongly reclaimed). Reproduced pre-fix (three SIGKILLed holders wedge a fourth run on "Roundtable seats full") and verified post-fix (the fourth run reclaims and proceeds; three LIVE holders are never reclaimed; benign init→sync→close passes; round-1 fixes untouched — confirmed by diff confinement in independent review).
- **overseer {skill_dir} (SKILL.md):** the placeholder was *defined* as the skill's references directory while its sole use appends `/references/prompt-templates.md`; the definition now denotes the skill root (the directory containing SKILL.md). Mechanical expansion against the real root now lands on the existing template file; the launch prompt itself is unchanged.
- **Rendering spec supply (prompt-templates.md):** the Phase 15.3 section now explicitly instructs the HTML agent to read SKILL.md's "Phase 15.3: Interactive HTML Report" section in full as binding, and carries a faithful summary of its mandates (10-section accordion with placeholders, Panel Gallery, filtering/sort, deep-linking, keyboard navigation, expand/collapse-all, print styles, height-bounded Chart.js wrappers, compressed-run banner, CDN libraries). Independent review enumerated 18 mandates from SKILL.md and confirmed every one reachable from the template section alone; the summary is headline-faithful, with sub-details reachable via the read-in-full instruction.

**Disclosed residual (pre-existing, outside the filed findings, NOT fixed here):** two Phase 15.3-output mandates live outside SKILL.md's named section — the HTML footer version string (in the Phase 15 Verification Gate's completion message) and the soft size-cap / slim-mode rule (in the closing Notes) — so the template section's pointer does not cover them. Noted for a future overseer edit round if the owner wants it.

**Branch currency:** main moved after this branch was cut (PR #82 vendored docs-mcp-server; PR #85 removed re0-upgrade under its RETIRE disposition). Per the second-merge rule noted on both PRs, main was merged into this branch (9c46ecc — the single conflict, the docs-lint exclusion line in ci.yml, was resolved as the union of both sides' exclusions) and the manifest was regenerated on the merged tree rather than hand-merged: scope is now 68 skills (main's 50 + this batch's 18), manifest 151 entries, checker clean. The fix commit then changed exactly three manifest lines.


---

## Addendum 2026-11-04 — round 3: the sync/close race fixed at the source (commit 0f51ff5)

The ae872dd review opened one further P2 in quest_helper.js: `sync` loaded a quest snapshot, made its GitHub call, then saved the whole snapshot — silently reverting a concurrent `close` (COMPLETED → ACTIVE, beads → PENDING). The owner directed a third fix round at the source; the file is re-copied byte-exact (live and repo sha256 `823119367a4d2987e498621aae2b1b1d32774bae905d1fdefe67131c8167b762`), manifest regenerated for the single file.

- **Fix:** optimistic re-validation with an atomic apply step. A new `QuestDB.updateQuest` performs fresh-load → mutate → store under the existing store lock; `sync` stamps only the `github_synced` field it owns onto the freshest stored quest and warns instead of stamping if the quest was re-initialized mid-flight (incarnation compared via `created_at`); `close` applies the same discipline to its own fields. No lock is held across the GitHub call, and no new locks were introduced.
- **Evidence:** reproduced pre-fix with a delayed `gh` stub (close persisted COMPLETED mid-flight; sync then reverted it, both commands exiting 0) and verified post-fix on both storage backends — the race now ends COMPLETED with sync's stamp applied on top and a concurrency note logged. Batteries: benign smokes on both paths, different-issue concurrency unaffected, round-1 invariants (injection titles inert; concurrent inits survive) and round-2 invariants (dead seats reclaimed, live seats never) all re-verified. Independent review: APPROVED-WITH-NOTES, including a call-site audit proving every wholesale JSON writer is reached only under the store lock.
- **Review notes, disclosed:** (1) on the Dolt backend, `updateQuest`'s serialization against the init path rests on Dolt's statement atomicity (the init writer is a single keyed REPLACE, unchanged from round 1) rather than the store lock; (2) the incarnation token's millisecond resolution makes a same-millisecond re-initialization theoretically indistinguishable — practically unreachable across process invocations, and benign (a stamp lands on the new incarnation). As in prior rounds, the Dolt backend is verified against a stub emulating the helper's queries — no real `dolt` binary exists in this environment; the JSON fallback path is verified end-to-end.


---

## Addendum 2026-11-04 — round 4: persistence failures propagate (commit fb74b0f); neurogenesis finding filed as #86

**Persistence fix.** The 0f51ff5 review found that a catch in the JSON store writer swallowed write failures: on a non-writable store, `close` exited 0 reporting COMPLETED while the stored quest stayed ACTIVE — and the same funnel served every JSON write, so `init` and `sync` made the same false claims. Fixed at the live source and re-copied byte-exact (live and repo sha256 `98ce7b4e330b52edb45597adc084b8ae7f0888304f2463ff917c2949ed160830`); the writer now throws and `main()` applies the file's fatal convention (Error + exit 1) before any success output is written. The implementer's nine-site catch audit and an independent re-derivation agree: the Dolt→JSON fallback catches (the fallback genuinely persists; its own failure now throws through), the read-side catches (degrade to fallback or a truthful not-found), the seat-owner catch (not quest persistence), the reviews-parse catch (fallback content is what gets persisted and reported), and the gh-failure catch (persists `github_synced:false` truthfully) are all correctly kept. Verified per command against a read-only store (run as an unprivileged user — this environment's root bypasses chmod): exit 1, no output file, store untouched; writable-again recovery clean; failed runs leave no wedged lock or seat.

**Reviewer residuals, disclosed and NOT fixed in this round (both pre-existing, both outside the round-4 class):** (1) cross-backend read shadowing — if a Dolt write fails while Dolt reads still succeed, a stale Dolt copy can shadow the newer JSON-fallback copy on later reads (the write itself is genuinely persisted); (2) the JSON writer's read-parse catch treats a corrupt-but-readable store as empty, so a rewrite can silently drop *other* quests from a corrupt store (the current quest is persisted and reported accurately). Recorded here for a future hardening decision.

**Neurogenesis finding:** per the owner's decision, the generated-orchestrator approval-flow defect in `skills/neurogenesis/SKILL.md` is filed as **issue #86** for its own deliberate fix round; its review thread is resolved against that issue.


---

## Addendum 2026-11-04 — round 5: atomic store publication (commit e81c253)

The fb74b0f review's remaining thread: JSON store updates were published by truncate-and-write in place, so a concurrent command's initial load could read a torn file and exit with a false "not found". Fixed at the live source and re-copied byte-exact (live and repo sha256 `5dbadb5808f5aaab1d533f6cfca14c16962c0ff5f04640de4e652b9e829faa94`); manifest regenerated for the single file.

- **Fix:** `_writeQuestToJson` serializes the full snapshot to `quest_db.json.tmp.<pid>` in the store's own directory, fsyncs it, and renames it over the store — readers only ever see complete snapshots. The replaced store preserves the previous file's permissions. Failures unlink the temp and propagate through round 4's unchanged error path (the store is never left truncated by a failed write).
- **Evidence:** torn reads under a concurrent reader/writer harness: 6/112 attempts pre-fix → 0/104 post-fix (implementer, 47.5 MB store), independently reproduced at 3/267 → 0/270 (reviewer, matched writer iterations). A planted stale temp is ignored by later runs; the rename-failure path (store path occupied by a directory) exits 1 with no litter and clean recovery. Independent review APPROVED-WITH-NOTES.
- **Deliberate semantics change, flagged per round 4:** atomic rename makes writability a directory property. A read-only store *file* (444) in a writable directory is now atomically replaced — the write genuinely succeeds, mode preserved (verified 444→444, 640→640) — while a read-only *directory* still fails loudly with no output file. Review notes: no directory fsync follows the rename (a power loss could revert to the previous *complete* snapshot, never a torn one; consistent with the file's conventions), and permission preservation is best-effort (an fchmod failure would leave the replacement at the default mode).
- **Residual status update:** round 4's disclosed residual (2) — the writer's read-parse catch treating a corrupt-but-readable store as empty — is narrowed by this fix: concurrency can no longer produce the corruption it would mishandle, and no reader path can cause data loss (parse failures degrade to loud exits or write-free aborts). The remaining exposure requires corruption from outside concurrency (manual edit, disk damage, a pre-round-5 torn file), after which the next write republishes with only its own quest. Residual (1) from round 4 (cross-backend read shadowing on the Dolt path) is unchanged. Both remain recorded here for a future hardening decision; neither blocks this batch under the owner's rounds 1–5 dispositions.


---

## Addendum 2026-11-04 — round 6: rule-skipped Phase 11 exempted from the overseer gate (commit fd7f9c7)

The e81c253 review also opened a thread on `skills/overseer/SKILL.md` (surfaced late in this PR's bookkeeping — see the round-6 note in the lane record; the finding itself is unaffected): the Edge Cases rule skips Phase 11 when a review has no P0/P1 findings, but the Phase 13.5 gate unconditionally required `phase_11_severity_verification.md`, so a correctly executed clean review failed the gate, burned a subagent re-dispatch, and could be mislabeled COMPRESSED RUN. The owner directed a fix at the source; the file is re-copied byte-exact (live and repo sha256 `09387af45f4193b5d9f6d1a02c77b524feccd4490f4cacc60eb367388c15451c`), manifest regenerated for the single file.

- **Fix:** the gate's Phase 11 bullet now carries a conditional-requirement annotation in the gate's own established style for skipped phases (cf. its Phase 5 row): the artifact is required only when Phase 11 ran; a skip under the Edge Cases rule is not a gate failure, is not re-dispatched, and never counts toward the COMPRESSED RUN determination. The Phase 11 definition, the skip rule, and the labeling rules are unchanged — a full census of the artifact name across the skill tree (5 occurrences, all in SKILL.md) confirmed the gate was the only passage attaching failure semantics to its absence; the remaining mentions are definitions, descriptive inventories, and input lists with no absence semantics.
- **Evidence:** both scenarios traced line-by-line pre- and post-fix, independently in review. Clean review: skip fires → gate passes without the artifact → no retry → no COMPRESSED RUN labeling. P0/P1 review (no weakening): Phase 11 runs, the artifact is required at full strength (existence / size / headers), and a missing or stub file still escalates to re-dispatch → unrecoverable → COMPRESSED RUN exactly as before. Reviewer notes: the annotation's lead clause keys on "ran", disambiguated by its second half, which scopes the exemption expressly to a rule-based skip (a crashed or dispatched-but-failed Phase 11 is not a skip and remains governed by the failure machinery); the Phase 14/14.5 input lists naming the artifact follow the document's established pattern for conditionally-skipped phases and are vacuous on a clean run.


---

## Addendum 2026-11-04 — round 7: seat cleanup made idempotent (commit 0cd18f0)

The fd7f9c7 review opened one thread in quest_helper.js's seat machinery (round 2's own remediation layer): the release cleanup could be invoked more than once for one process — `main()`'s finally block, the registered exit hook, and the signal handlers all reach it — and a second invocation landing after another process had reacquired the seat deleted the *new* owner's seat, bypassing the three-instance limit (reproduced: A releases, B acquires, A's cleanup re-runs, B's ownership vanishes, C takes B's seat). The owner directed a fix; the file is re-copied byte-exact (live and repo sha256 `0ab3b64db07e78483e2c2a73d0cc47039cd7d1505b0151b8013aa57c5966664c`), manifest regenerated for the single file.

- **Fix:** the release closure in `acquireConcurrencySlot` now no-ops after its first invocation (a per-acquisition `released` guard), and additionally skips deletion when the owner record names a different process — closing the reclaim-and-reacquire route to the same harm while still freeing record-less seats. All four invocation sites funnel through this single closure; a full audit confirms only two seat-deleting sites exist in the file (this closure and round 2's `tryReclaimSeat`, untouched).
- **Evidence:** the A/B/C interleave reproduced pre-fix and inverted post-fix in independent review (the new owner's seat and owner record byte-identical after the stale second cleanup; the third process blocks until the real owner releases). Signal paths (SIGINT/SIGTERM via main()'s exact wiring) free the seat exactly once; the SIGKILL path still relies on round-2 reclaim. Independent review APPROVED-WITH-NOTES: the re-check deliberately falls through to deletion on a missing/unreadable record (the correct trade — the acquisition-time owner write is best-effort, so the strict form would leak write-failed seats until staleness), making the guard the primary defense and the re-check defense-in-depth.
- **Assessed residual, not fixed (recorded in the round record):** one triple conjunction survives — this process's owner write fails at acquisition AND its record-less seat is staleness-reclaimed and reacquired AND the delete lands inside the reacquirer's mkdir→owner-write microsecond gap. Its impact is bounded to the three-instance seat limit; the store lock and atomic publication are independent mechanisms. Both the implementer and the reviewer judged "assessed, not fixed" the right call at this scope.


---

## Addendum 2026-11-04 — round 8: empty reviews preserved, no fabricated beads (commit 2447dfd)

The 0cd18f0 review opened one thread in quest_helper.js's init path: a valid clean review ({"findings":[]}) was indistinguishable from omitted review input, so init substituted three hard-coded sample remediation beads (including CRITICAL and HIGH items unrelated to the repository) onto an ACTIVE quest, and a later sync published them to the GitHub issue. The owner directed a fix; the file is re-copied byte-exact (live and repo sha256 `43393a85ebcbee493c7a70d8e1481b04c31fa60644a090a741746a5d0aee8896`), manifest regenerated for the single file.

- **Fix:** `runInit` now sets a `reviewsLoaded` flag only after a provided reviews file parses and its findings map successfully; the default-bead fallback requires that flag unset. A loaded empty review persists zero beads with an explicit clean-review message ("no remediation is needed", stderr); the quest is created ACTIVE with `beads: []`, close finalizes it normally, and sync publishes a truthful header-only comment.
- **Preserved behavior (the contract's other half):** omitted `--reviews-path` and malformed reviews files produce exactly the pre-fix fallback — verified programmatically identical to the pre-fix copy in independent review, stderr text included. A parseable file with no `findings` field also keeps the fallback (the findings array is the defining shape of a review this tool consumes; treating a field-less file as an authoritative clean review would silently swallow malformed producer output).
- **Disclosed residual (independent review, low, pre-existing, unchanged by this fix):** a NONEXISTENT `--reviews-path` is silently treated as omitted input — the existsSync gate skips loading without a warning and the default beads are substituted, the same fabrication outcome via an operator typo. Byte-identical to the pre-fix copy and outside this finding's scope; recorded here so the disposition is on the record.


---

## Addendum 2026-11-04 — round 9: seat reclamation serialized against reacquisition (commit d418aeb)

The 0cd18f0 review also opened (in a trailing post, minutes after the review completed) a race in `tryReclaimSeat`: its abandonment check and its deletion were not atomic — two waiters inspecting the same dead owner's seat could both pass the check, and the slower one's deletion removed the seat a faster reclaimer had already re-acquired for a new live owner. The owner directed a fix; the file is re-copied byte-exact (live and repo sha256 `1c05ecf6d26afbb32dc4bc58aaed24974682ef997ded20c672f8a837fdd41c99`), manifest regenerated for the single file.

- **Fix:** reclamation now claims the seat directory with an atomic rename to a unique sibling name (`lock_N.reclaim.<pid>`): a concurrent loser sees the rename fail and backs off. The winner re-validates abandonment on the claimed directory and deletes only there; a claimed directory that turns out to be a re-acquired live seat is renamed back untouched and the reclaim reports failure. Abandonment semantics (recorded-owner liveness via kill(pid, 0), the 30 s record-less staleness rule) are unchanged — the predicate was extracted verbatim. Trash directories orphaned by a winner crashing mid-delete are deliberately left unswept (the seat scan only considers the numbered names; a sweeper would need its own coordination).
- **Evidence:** both interleave orders independently verified (resume-before-reacquisition: exactly one reclaim succeeds; resume-after: the live owner's directory is restored at the original path with its owner record byte-identical and a third helper blocks). Uncontended SIGKILL reclaim through the real CLI is unchanged; a live seat survives sequential and concurrent reclaim attempts. Independent review APPROVED-WITH-NOTES.
- **Assessed residual, stated precisely (independent review corrected an earlier, stronger draft of this claim):** in a double-nested window — the check-to-rename gap spanning a complete reclaim AND reacquisition, plus a further acquisition landing inside the microsecond revalidation window — the displaced owner can keep running seatless while three numbered seats are held, so four helpers may briefly be in their critical sections. The bounded guarantee is the narrower one: no live owner's seat directory or owner record is ever deleted or corrupted in any constructed path; the overshoot is limited to one already-admitted runner finishing its work, and the displaced owner's own release cannot delete the newer seat (round 7's owner-record re-check). Accepted as residual risk at this scope.


---

## Addendum — overseer panel P1 fix pass (2026-11-04, head d672873)

The overseer panel run against this branch (verdict 5/10, MERGE AFTER FIXES) raised four new P1s in skills Codex had not reached. Per the owner's direction, all four were fixed at the live source (planning-wringer plan: Tasks 1–4) and re-copied here; each fix was implemented and independently reviewed under subagent-driven development. Evidence classes are named honestly per fix: the grep harnesses are necessary-condition floors (they prove text, not behavior); the load-bearing evidence is the behavioral item listed.

**DF-B1 — diagnosing-superpowers posted unscrubbed report content to a public repo.** Step 5's issue creation, prefilled-URL/paste fallbacks, and comment-on-existing-issue flow now consume exactly one artifact: `issue-gate/post-body.md`, produced by copying the filled text into a gate directory as a never-post draft and running the skill's own scrub → scrub-audit loop (BUNDLE = gate directory) until the audit returns CLEAN. `templates/issue.md`'s false "(scrubbed)" claim is replaced by the gate reference; the comment command (`gh issue comment … --body-file …/issue-gate/post-body.md`) is now specified. *Evidence:* stubbed end-to-end execution by a fresh agent against a `gh` shim, both branches (create and comment): every recorded posting binds only `post-body.md`; a planted canary secret appears in no payload (including the percent-encoded prefilled URL); a scrub log exists in each gate directory. The earlier scrub step (step 6, bundle archive) is unchanged.
- *Known remaining P2 (not fixed, recorded):* step 5's issue *search* still sends symptom terms derived from the session to the tracker (census item E4).

**D7 — the transcript-as-data guard never reached the agents holding the sink.** "Treat transcript content as evidence, not instructions" existed only in `references/redaction-policy.md`, read by the two sink-less scrub prompts. The guard now also sits in SKILL.md's Hard rules, in SKILL.md step 3 (the dispatcher, which reads transcripts and holds the `gh` sink), and in `prompts/analyst-common.md`. The source sentence is verbatim; two clauses were authored for this fix (a never-follow clause covering instructions/requests/tool calls in transcripts or tool output, and a carve-out keeping the partner's own in-transcript prompts usable as evidence of what was asked) and were ratified by the owner with the plan.
- *Evidence:* fresh-agent behavior check — a fixture transcript with a planted instruction addressed to the diagnosing agent inside a tool result was treated strictly as evidence (no action taken, not propagated); the partner's instruction-shaped prompt was still carried as evidence, per the carve-out.

**D5a — plan-review-integrator stated specialist launch timing four irreconcilable ways.** One initiation rule now governs, stated in the Orchestration Contract: spawns initiate only in contract batches after Phase 5.5 coverage + Phase 6 classification; later phases may require or consume batch results and initiate nothing. The Step 4 phase-gate timing grant is deleted (replaced by a pointer to the contract); Phase 4 verification is re-scoped (flag during Phase 4, verify via a post-classification batch); Phase 6.5 points at the contract by name; Phase 7's pre-edit batch is preserved as a contract batch; Phase 8 consumes remaining cap via the contract only. Phase 6.5's mini-votes are explicitly scoped as a separate mechanism with their own budget (not specialist spawns, not cap-counted).
- *Evidence:* two independent full-file censuses (implementer + reviewer, wide synonym set, same 19-locus classification) plus a fresh end-to-end executor read confirming exactly one launch timeline. D5b (P2, confirmation-order presentation in the same skill) is **not** fixed here: it defaults to file-with-owner at the merge report — its honest fix relocates a gate across phases and needs its own small plan.

**D6 — overseer's Phase 13.5 gate cited required-section lists that did not exist.** The lists now exist in `references/prompt-templates.md` (the file the gate already points to; overseer SKILL.md is content-unchanged in this pass apart from fork markers): one list per gated file type (7), every entry derived from SKILL.md's phase section, the phase's prompt skeleton, or the gate text itself, with match semantics stated (operative noun phrase, case-insensitive) and non-coverage recorded (round 2/3 files, Phase 6 summaries).
- *Evidence:* fixture pair — the panel's own 27 state artifacts: 21 pass; a header-stripped copy fails. **Recorded residual:** all 6 Phase 5 round-1 fixtures fail the honestly derived list (17 entries): Phase 5's sources mandate debate *content* but name no section headers, while real artifacts carry the content under headers no source names (`## Positions` / `## Concessions` / `## Holds` / `## New Discoveries`). The list was not loosened to fit. The defect is now detectable and recorded instead of silent, but fully closing it requires naming Phase 5 headers in overseer SKILL.md / its skeleton — an owner decision item at the merge report.

**Fork-version marking (owner instruction, 2026-11-04).** All three skills touched by this pass now carry explicit fork marking vs their source origins: `fork_of:` + `fork_version: 1` in SKILL.md frontmatter, and a `FORK.md` in each skill directory recording source origin, origin pin/version (overseer's 3.2.0 and plan-review-integrator's 2.1.0 are the origin versions and are unchanged), fork version, and a dated change log. Five other locally modified skills were marked the same way at the live source today; their markers reach the repo via the normal skill-sync path. Directory names are unchanged (skills resolve by name).

**Notes.** Per D4 amendment A1, these live-source edits took effect in the live environment when made, before this re-copy. D8 (P2: CI executes neither of the branch's two executables — `node --check` for quest_helper.js and shell-lint coverage for wizard's template.sh, which currently carries 16 shellcheck findings) is **not** fixed here; it defaults to file-with-owner at the merge report.


---

## Addendum — repair round: Phase 10 vocabulary semantics (2026-11-04, head 7291f5a)

Codex's review of the panel-P1 head (d672873, CI 7/7) raised one P2, a genuine defect in the D6 lists as first shipped: the Phase 10 entry required **all five** classification labels to occur in a claim-verification report, while SKILL.md mandates classifying *each* claim with *a* label from that vocabulary — an all-`[VERIFIED]` report is complete, yet the gate would have rejected it and risked a false COMPRESSED RUN marking. Fixed at the source and re-copied (b5cc3c7): the five per-label bullets are now a single `(vocabulary)` entry (any one label satisfies presence; an all-same-label report is explicitly complete) plus a preamble defining the gate semantics — presence (≥1 classification), conformance (no assigned label outside the set), read from the report's Verdict column, with quoted tokens from other phases counting neither way. All seven lists were audited for the same every-outcome fallacy; it was present only in Phase 10 (Phase 3 severity tags and Phase 11 `[EXISTING_DEFECT]|[PLAN_RISK]` were already alternation). Evidence: synthetic fixtures — all-`[VERIFIED]` passes, no-labels fails presence, out-of-vocabulary verdict fails conformance; the panel's real Phase 10 fixture passes presence+conformance; against the previous text the all-verified case fails with exactly the four absent labels (the defect reproduced). The Codex thread was answered with this disposition and resolved. Independent review APPROVED-WITH-NOTES with two recorded limits of a headers-level gate, disclosed rather than fixed: (i) presence+conformance cannot detect *partial* classification (a report classifying only some claims passes — the same structural limit the 13.5 gate has for every phase); (ii) a bracketed token quoted *inside* a Verdict cell is collected as a classification, where a preamble-following gatekeeper would discount it (edge case, no real fixture affected).
